Figure1: province [N]; coordinates_a_km [Na,2], coordinates_b_km [Nb,2] in the same projected CRS; cell_size_km scalar. Outputs counts and shared grid cells. Geographic coordinates use workflows/grid_overlap.py with bundled boundaries and the original Miller grid.
Figure3: HH, LL, HL, LH, MHH, MLL [group N,2]: positive/negative ROI means with identical row ordering. Bootstrap HH/LL with replacement at min(N_HL,N_LH), sharing indices across ROI signs; equal-tail two-sided p.
ExtendedDataFigure1: measurements [N,V], province [N], measurement_labels [V]. Generates ANOVA/ICC tables. Item-level rwg and Cronbach alpha are in analyses/psychometrics.py and cultural_pca.py; demographic tabulations require supplied variables.

ExtendedDataFigure6: cortex [N,R], culture [N,M], province [N], correlation_method scalar string pearson or spearman; gradients [R,K], spin_indices [S,R]. Province-mean signed RDMs; the same correlation method is used for observations and unrestricted label shuffles.
ExtendedDataFigure9: correlation_draws [B,P,S], proportions [P], series_labels [S]. Median and percentile ribbons from supplied refitted maps. Resampling/refit helpers: china/run_sensitivity.m and refit_sample.m.

ExtendedDataFigure15: china_correlations and world_correlations [joint PCs, local PCs], at least 2x2. Axis angles use the first two joint-PC coordinates and acute angles between axes. Obtain correlations from aligned joint/local PCA scores.
SupplementaryFigure1: word_scores [G,S], validity_score [G], score_labels [S]. Validity scatters; raw daily word-index cleaning and weighted PCA run through analyses/run_word_pipeline.py first. Dictionary labels are caller-supplied.
SupplementaryFigure2: participant1 and participant2 [C,R], center_labels [C]. Both matrices must be aligned to the SAME shared centers/ROIs, with finite positive thickness. Uses leave-one-center medians and transfers calibration between participants. Additional nonshared centers must be handled separately for descriptive maps.
SupplementaryFigure3: components [C], statistics [C,S], series_labels [S]. For complete synthetic source data and the dedicated plotter use simulation/generate_si3.m, export_si3_source.py and plot_si3.m.
